column15: Kentucky straight bourbon (Clermont, KY); flavored line (Apple etc.) is still bourbon-based. Bourbon category confirmed peat-free by production process (charred new oak, no peat smoke).
Core "Bruichladdich" range (Classic Laddie etc.) is explicitly unpeated per source. Siblings Octomore and Port Charlotte are separate rows below, never averaged into this one.
Super-heavily peated - described as the most heavily peated whisky in the world (100-300+ ppm). Named directly in this batch's Bruichladdich sample products ("Octomore 13.3").

Heavily peated (~40ppm) Bruichladdich sibling brand. Not itself in this batch's 6 sampled product names, but a well-documented sibling explicitly flagged as a "known pair to watch" in the research brief; added so it never inherits the unpeated core-range profile.

Core range (DoubleWood, PortWood, Montilla, 12/14/17/21) is unpeated. Distillery restarted an annual one-week peated malting run in 2001 ("Peat Week"); those limited releases (Peat Week, Peated Triple Cask, Week of Peat) are heavily peated - see rule rows.

Source confirms Speyside location and Campari ownership but does not use the word "unpeated" explicitly; classic light/fruity unpeated Speyside style is the standard consensus. Confidence kept low because the fetched text did not state the peat claim outright.

Highland distillery in Blackford, Perth and Kinross, owned by Picard Vins & Spiritueux (Terroirs Distillers) since 2011. Source describes cask-finish range but does not explicitly state "unpeated"; kept low confidence for that reason.

French single malt, founded 2022, distilled at Distillerie Tessendier (Maison Boinaud) in Jarnac, Charente. Site lists a "Peated" expression (French: Tourbe) as a distinct product from "Original", implying the core/Original line is unpeated - see rule row for the peated "Tourbe" expression. Intensity of Tourbe not confirmed with ppm data.
Kentucky straight bourbon, currently distilled at Lux Row Distillers in Bardstown, KY (Luxco/MGP Ingredients).

Bardstown, KY distillery owned by Luxco/MGP Ingredients; produces Ezra Brooks (unpeated, see that row) among other bourbon brands. defaultTypeName left empty since the site produces more than one whiskey type; peatProfile left unknown at this distillery-level row since it is effectively a multi-brand bottling site rather than one house style.

Chicago craft distillery, certified organic and kosher. Source confirms the distillery and its organic/craft positioning but does not explicitly state "unpeated"; American grain whiskeys (rye, single barrel, millet) are not malted-and-peated in the Scotch sense, so peatProfile=none with low confidence. defaultTypeName left empty (range spans rye/other grains).
The only widely-available peated Irish single malt. Distilled at Cooley. Phenol level reported ~14-15 ppm - clearly peated but well below Islay heavyweights, so classed medium rather than heavy.

Main output (Tyrconnell, Kilbeggan, 2 Gingers) is unpeated; Connemara is the peated exception, modelled as a separate brand row (parentSlug=cooley) rather than averaged in. defaultTypeName left empty since the site makes single malt, blended and grain whiskey.

Knockdhu distillery. Modern core range is unpeated (evolved from an originally peaty 1894 style); since 2014 a separate "Peaty Collection" (Cutter, Flaughter, Tushkar, Peatheart, Sherry Cask Finish Peated Edition) uses malt peated to ~20ppm - see rule row. Region recorded as Highland (Knock, Aberdeenshire, near the Speyside boundary); some sources place it in Speyside instead - low-confidence detail flagged for reviewer, though it does not affect the peat call.

Fife (near St Andrews) Lowland distillery, opened 2014/2015. No page opened this session to cite a peat claim (Lowland single malt is conventionally unpeated, and none of this batch's 6 sample product names suggest otherwise), so peatProfile is correctly left unknown per the citation rule rather than asserting an uncited "none". A reviewer can very likely confirm none with a quick lookup.
Islay's newest distillery (opened 2019), owned by Hunter Laing. Standard malt spec is 40ppm phenol, comparable to Port Charlotte's 40ppm (recorded heavy in this batch).

Could not identify this brand: WebSearch budget was exhausted early in this session and no working URL could be guessed for it via WebFetch. Sample names ("Fuyu Mizunara", "Fuyu Sochu Small Batch Barley") suggest a Japanese-styled malt but this is unconfirmed. 5 products - flagged for a human reviewer with search access.

Canadian spiced/flavored whisky (Cinnamon, Pumpkin, Ginger Bread, Chocolat editions); maker confirmed via the samples themselves ("Maison des Futailles Spicebox ..."). The official spiceboxwhisky domain no longer resolves to the brand (parked/expired), so the peat claim is only backed by the general Canadian-whisky category page, which does not discuss peat explicitly - kept low confidence.

No web presence found for this exact brand; "Glen"-prefixed name strongly suggests a generic/own-label Scotch blend for this market (4 products, all just "Glen Angel" with no descriptors). Treated per the long-tail own-label default: ordinary blended Scotch is conventionally unpeated.

Israel's first whisky distillery (Tel Aviv, founded 2013). The "Elements" range (Sherry Cask, Red Wine Cask, Peated) is this distillery's own-brand line, so modelled as one producer rather than a separate "M&H Elements" brand row. Baseline (non-Peated Elements editions) is unpeated; the Peated Cask edition gets its smokiness from maturation in ex-Islay (peated-whisky) casks rather than peated malt itself - see rule row, and note it is real cask-derived peat character, not just a marketing name.

Highland distillery in Alness, owned by Diageo; mainly produces malt for blending (Johnnie Walker Red Label). Source does not explicitly say "unpeated" so confidence kept low, though this is standard for a Diageo Highland blending malt.

Douglas Laing's regional "Remarkable Regional Malts" range - single-cask/small-batch bottlings labelled by region (Islay, Highland, Speyside, and others). Some regions are sold as single malt, others as blended malt on Douglas Laing's own site, which this batch's plain "Clan Denny Islay/Highland/Speyside" sample names cannot disambiguate - defaultTypeName left empty. Baseline set to unpeated for the Highland/Speyside editions (not explicitly confirmed for those two individually); the Islay edition is a heavily peated exception - see rule row.
Independent bottler/blender, Glasgow, established 1948 by Fred Douglas Laing. Owns the Big Peat, Rock Island and Clan Denny ranges in this batch. Bottler rows carry no house peat level by definition.

Oldmeldrum, Aberdeenshire. Peated on its own malt floors until 1995; reopened unpeated in 1997 and "today the malt floors are closed and Glen Garioch follows a different style, only occasionally peaty whiskies are produced." Modern core range (Founder's Reserve, 12yo etc., matching this batch's samples) is unpeated.

Arran's second distillery (opened 2019), a separate physical site from Arran/Lochranza - built specifically to produce a heavily peated style (50ppm Highland peat), unlike unpeated Arran. Region islands/legalRegion highland per the same Arran convention as Tobermory.

Could not identify this brand (WebSearch budget exhausted, no working URL found via WebFetch). All 3 sample names are just "River Proof Series" with no other descriptor - flagged for a human reviewer with search access; "Proof" naming hints at American whiskey but this is a guess, not asserted in any field.

Catalogue brand string is "Whisky of Voodoo" but every sampled product actually reads "Spirit of Voodoo ..." - modelled under the real product-line name with both spellings aliased. Could not identify the producer/country (WebSearch budget exhausted; the guessed domain spiritofvoodoo.com does not resolve). Flagged for a human reviewer.

Historic London wine & spirits merchant and independent bottler (BBR range), est. 1698 - well-established general knowledge, but no page was opened for it this session, so left without sourceUrls and confidence dropped to low accordingly (peatProfile is correctly unknown for a bottler regardless). Sample "Berry Bros. Lochindaal 2010 Cask #4339" - "Lochindaal" could not be confirmed as a historical Bruichladdich brand name this session (the Bruichladdich Wikipedia article does not mention it), so no separate Lochindaal row was created; a reviewer familiar with Bruichladdich's older naming should check this.

Named in Berry Bros.' sample product ("Longmorn Cask.71768 Berrys'"), added per the independent-bottler rule. Source confirms Speyside location and Chivas Brothers/Pernod Ricard ownership but does not explicitly state "unpeated"; standard consensus for this distillery is unpeated, kept low confidence for the missing explicit statement.

Small American bourbon label ("1843", "Reserve"). Could not confirm the current producing distillery this session (no working page found); kind=blend used as the safe default for a sourced/undisclosed-distillery American whiskey label rather than asserting a specific parent. peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category fact, not a brand-specific source.

Slow Hand / "Slow Hand Organic" whiskey. Could not open a working source this session (official-domain guess failed on a TLS handshake error, WebSearch budget was already exhausted) - left fully unknown rather than rely on unverified recollection. Only 2 products; low priority but flagged in case a reviewer has a source handy.

Glengyle distillery, sister operation to Springbank under J&A Mitchell. Owner/region confirmed via Wikipedia, but no opened source stated the standard range's peat level despite several attempts (whisky.com and masterofmalt both blocked the fetch with 403). Kilkerran's standard bottlings are widely reputed to be lightly peated, and this batch's own sample ("Kilkerran Heavily Peated") shows a distinctly heavier release exists separately - see the rule row for that one product name, added without an external citation since the name is self-declaring. A human reviewer with access to whisky.com or the distillery's own site should confirm the baseline peat level and promote it off "unknown".

Smoke Symphony and "Orchard Outburst" - could not identify this brand this session (WebSearch budget exhausted, no working URL guessed). "Smoke Symphony" naming hints at a possible smoky/peated expression, which is exactly why it is left unknown rather than guessed - flagged for a human reviewer.
No web presence found; generic "Scottish"-branded name, 2 products with no descriptors - treated per the long-tail own-label default (ordinary blended Scotch is conventionally unpeated).

Sample name "Eigashima Shuzo Tokinoka White Oak Distillery" is strong self-evidence that Tokinoka is a label of Eigashima Shuzo's White Oak (Akashi) distillery - Eigashima Shuzo's existence and operation of White Oak was confirmed via Wikipedia (see the eigashima row), but that source does not mention "Tokinoka" by name or discuss peat, so left without its own sourceUrls and peatProfile=unknown rather than assumed.
Runs the White Oak distillery in Akashi, Japan ("Akashi" branded whisky since 2007). Parent for the Tokinoka brand in this batch. Peat level not stated in the source, left unknown.
North Wales single malt distillery (first in North Wales since the early 1900s). Official site does not explicitly say "unpeated", so confidence kept low despite no indication of peat use.
Blended malt of only Islay whiskies (Ardbeg, Port Ellen, Bowmore, Caol Ila) at 46% - all heavily peated Islay distilleries.
Single-product own label; could not identify this brand this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). Fast/cheap long-tail treatment per the brief; left fully unknown rather than guessed.
Glen Barley №3, single product, generic "Glen"-prefixed own-label name typical of this market's cheap Scotch blends - treated per the long-tail own-label default.

Single-product brand; could not identify a source this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). "Hinotori" (火鳥, "firebird") is an unambiguous Japanese word, so countryCode is guessed as JP on that basis alone - this guess is NOT backed by a citation and peatProfile is correctly left unknown; a reviewer should verify the brand entirely.
Willett small-batch bourbon label, Bardstown, KY.
Willett small-batch bourbon label, Bardstown, KY.
Bardstown, KY. Parent distillery for Kentucky Vintage and Noah's Mill in this batch. defaultTypeName left empty - Willett bottles both bourbon and rye whiskey.

McCarthy's Oregon Single Malt Whiskey, made at Clear Creek Distillery (Hood River, Oregon) - confirmed via Wikipedia's Clear Creek Distillery article. That article does not discuss peat, and no other working source could be reached this session (McCarthy's own Wikipedia page and a distiller.com guess both 404/403'd; clearcreekdistillery.com failed TLS verification). McCarthy's is WIDELY reported in whiskey literature as made with malt imported from Scotland and heavily peated (commonly cited around 50ppm) - this is exactly the kind of positive peat claim the brief asks to flag: I could not verify it with an opened source this session, so it is left peatProfile=unknown rather than asserted. A human reviewer should very likely resolve this to heavy/medium with a proper citation.

Hood River, Oregon (formerly Portland). Also makes fruit brandies and liqueurs alongside McCarthy's whiskey, so defaultTypeName left empty and peatProfile left unknown at the distillery level (see the mccarthys row for the specific, unresolved peat question).

Heaven Hill's annual limited-edition bourbon/rye/wheat series named for Parker Beam. defaultTypeName left empty since editions vary by grain/type year to year; all are American whiskey, hence unpeated.

Private family-owned Kentucky straight bourbon distillery. Parent for Parker's Heritage Collection in this batch. defaultTypeName left empty (bourbon and rye both produced); peatProfile=none since American straight whiskey is categorically unpeated (confirmed via the bourbon category source), consistent with the child brand row.

Blended malt combining single malts from Islay, Arran, Jura and Orkney (formerly "Rock Oyster"). Source confirms the composition but does not describe smoke/peat intensity; since only one of the four source islands (Islay) is reliably peated and the others are unpeated/lightly peated, "light" is a conservative estimate, not a confirmed figure - kept low confidence, flagged for a reviewer.

Single-product own label; could not identify a source this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). The name itself suggests possible smokiness/peat, which is exactly why it is left unknown rather than guessed - flagged for a human reviewer.

Suntory's "forest distillery" in Yamanashi. Source lists a "Heavily Peated" 2013 limited series as distinct from the core range (which includes the "Distiller's Reserve" in this batch's sample), implying the standard range is milder - but the source does not explicitly grade the core range's own peat level, so this is an inference. Recorded as light with low confidence rather than none, since Hakushu's standard style is commonly described as having a faint smokiness distinct from Yamazaki's unpeated style.
Single-product own label; could not identify a source this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). Generic English word as a brand name - left fully unknown.
